headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance exposure: Copilot can read repo context while next-ai-draw-io uses broad network/MCP and third-party APIs, creating unsafe cross-tool data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and uses MCP/browser-backed workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if content from one is copied into the other or shared through files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF content from Copilot-generated files is pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests diagram text or document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a manual review step before copying any generated text between tools
Prefix imported content with a fixed delimiter and treat it as data only
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported snippets
requires-engineering: isolate the two tools in separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and open buffers, and next-ai-draw-io can send content to multiple third-party model APIs with broad network egress. If the same workspace contains sensitive code or documents, data can flow from Copilot-visible files into next-ai-draw-io outputs or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets, source code, or confidential documents
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a hosted model provider rather than local-only inference
mitigations: Keep sensitive repos and diagram inputs in separate folders
Use local-only models in next-ai-draw-io for confidential material
Remove secrets from open buffers before invoking either tool
Rotate any API keys exposed to next-ai-draw-io prompts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while next-ai-draw-io can also mutate files and diagrams through its document-processing workflow. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent edits to the same workspace can conflict even without shell access. The overlap is real but not inherently irreversible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or diagram file concurrently
IF git changes from Copilot are saved while next-ai-draw-io rewrites the same asset
mitigations: Use one editor session per file at a time
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same workspace
Commit or snapshot changes before switching tools
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: route edits through a single orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code and workspace edits that next-ai-draw-io can ingest as document content or diagram text. If next-ai-draw-io treats that output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. There is no documented verification loop between the pair, so the interaction is plausible and should be rated medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io imports Copilot-generated text without validation
IF a diagram or document is regenerated from Copilot output and then reused as source
mitigations: Require human review before reusing generated text
Compare regenerated diagrams against source files
Mark AI-generated sections clearly in the workspace
requires-engineering: add checksum-based verification between tools
requires-engineering: block direct action on unreviewed AI output

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and vendor APIs, while next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and can call multiple external model providers. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create residency and retention mismatches plus third-party disclosure risk. Because the profiles do not document matching compliance controls, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF GitHub repo context includes data subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either tool
Use tenant-approved model endpoints only
Remove API keys from prompts and diagrams
requires-engineering: document retention and residency boundaries
requires-engineering: add compliance gating before external API calls
